summary: Retrospective after last week's regression where a model version rollout caused elevated tail latency and a small percentage of requests to error. Focus was on root cause hypotheses (KV cache invalidation + model pin mismatch), immediate rollback rationale, and a concrete fallback/canary plan plus action items for deeper forensic logs and legal access requests.
topics: fallback policy (model variant fallback vs. region failover)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight — 47 minutes on the calendar — and the goal is to close out the follow ups from the regression last thursday.
[00:18] Diego Alvarez: yep, thanks. we got pulled into the incident channel pretty quick but still seeing residual 5xxs from the spike window, so want to understand root cause and next steps.
[00:32] Rohit Patel: quick recap from our side — we saw a canary rollout that bumped model X.v12 into production. about 2.3% of traffic was routed to the new variant, after ~12 hours the tail p50->p99 latency diverged and error rates climbed to ~0.6%. we rolled back to v11 at 09:42 and error rates dropped.
[00:57] Priya Singh: two quick clarifications — the rollout was via Dedicated pool in us-west-2 with prefix caching enabled, correct?
[01:05] Rohit Patel: correct, dedicated, prefix/kv cache was on. also there was concurrent autoscale event on the node pool which increased instance count.
[01:18] Marcus Lee: we've captured the alerts, and SRE timeline shows the spike lines up with several cache invalidations — sometimes the cache TTLs reset when the model hash didn't match. could be a model pin mismatch or serialization change.
[01:33] Diego Alvarez: when you say serialization change, do you mean tokenization or the model checkpoint layout?
[01:38] Rohit Patel: likely checkpoint layout/kv cache key namespace changed — small change in tokenizer metadata caused different prefix hashes which ended up bypassing the existing KV entries; that plus a burst of cold-starts pushed latency up.
[01:54] Maya Chen: I want to flag that some of the transcripts and logs have weird names for the product — the auto transcription shows "Redwood dedicate" and "key-v cash" — so please ignore those typos in the exported logs.
[02:08] Priya Singh: haha yeah the fireflies transcript is creative.
[02:14] Rohit Patel: we've attached a draft postmortem doc (link) that contains the timeline, metric plots, and an initial hypothesis section. it's marked as draft because we need matching request ids and payloads from BlueArc to validate.
[02:29] Diego Alvarez: action: we'll upload the batch of failing request ids — roughly 6k ids from the window — but some are redacted, we'll provide a mapping.
[02:40] Maya Chen: great. moving to fallback strategy: we want to confirm what you prefer — automatic model fallback to a pin-compatible variant or a region-based failover? each has tradeoffs: model fallback keeps latency stable but might produce slightly lower quality; region failover reduces capacity strain but adds egress latency.
[03:05] Marcus Lee: leaning model fallback. we can't afford cross-region hop for our low-latency features.
[03:13] Rohit Patel: ok model fallback then — operationally we recommend a 2-tier fallback: primary exact-pin, fallback to quantized v11-alpha variant, fallback #2 to smaller architecture in same pool. that gives both latency and continuity.
[03:32] Priya Singh: will that be automatic or manual? during the regression we manually rolled back, that took too long.
[03:39] Rohit Patel: we can set policy: automatic degrade-on-latency-sla breach for 30s window and automatic rollback if errors exceed 0.3% for 5 minutes, with an immediate page to on-call. we need your approval to enable automatic rollback for account BA-0421.
[03:58] Diego Alvarez: need to discuss with ops, but likely yes if we get guardrails and the canary is smaller.
[04:07] Maya Chen: speaking of canary, proposed canary plan in canary-plan.xlsx: 1% traffic for 24h, KV-cache off during initial 2h, then re-enable if stable, synthetic traffic ramp at 5% after 12h.
[04:25] Priya Singh: can you clarify "KV-cache off" — does Redwood have a toggle per deployment?
[04:31] Rohit Patel: yes, we expose a runtime flag per route: prefix_cache_enabled: true/false. turning it off forces cold starts and bypasses prefix hits which helps validate the model-change independent of cache behavior.
[04:47] Marcus Lee: that's helpful. can you also expose a per-instance debug log level to capture kv keys? we need those for the audit.
[04:55] Rohit Patel: we can do debug-level kv logging but it's high volume, which ties to retention and cost — need legal sign-off for extended retention.
[05:05] Lena Park: I'll coordinate legal for extended log access; we want the logs but also to limit exposure.
[05:12] Diego Alvarez: question on observability: why didn't the trace sampler catch the slow call paths earlier?
[05:18] Rohit Patel: two reasons: our sampling was 0.5% for that route and the affected requests were a small tail population, and secondly, the telemetry pipeline had a transient ingestion lag (we documented it in the postmortem). we propose increasing route-specific sampler to 5% for the next 72h during the canary.
[05:38] Priya Singh: acceptable for the test window.
[05:41] Maya Chen: let's put that as an action item. Rohit, can you scope expected log size and cost delta?
[05:47] Rohit Patel: early estimate: enabling kv debug logs for the 24h canary will increase log volume by ~12GB/day and about $125/day in ingestion for your account tier — rough numbers.
[06:00] Diego Alvarez: we can cover that during the pilot.
[06:05] Priya Singh: there was also mention in the internal thread that the rollout script uses model hash matching against a manifest — any chance manifest mismatch caused a mis-route?
[06:14] Rohit Patel: good point — we've found one case where manifest was regenerated with different ordering which changed the content-hash. we have a fix: manifest hash will be canonicalized by sorting keys before hashing.
[06:27] Marcus Lee: ok, that explains intermittent mismatches.
[06:31] Maya Chen: also want to discuss SLA ramifications: this caused a partial degradation but not full outage. our SLA impacts are in the doc, and we'll provide credit calculations if the incident qualifies.
[06:43] Diego Alvarez: we'll take that under advisement — finance will want the breakdown.
[06:47] Rohit Patel: quick pointer: some of the transcribed terms in the logs show Kubernetes as 'Cube-ernates' — please ignore transcription misses.
[06:55] Priya Singh: noted.
[07:00] Maya Chen: moving onto the rollback decision: we rolled back because error rate was rising and user-facing SLOs were breached. the team debated throttling instead — any notes on why rollback was chosen over throttling?
[07:12] Marcus Lee: throttling would've kept more traffic but still risked degraded responses; rollback gave immediate stability and we could observe whether errors receded. throttling wasn't implemented because of risk to downstream ops.
[07:25] Rohit Patel: also, throttling would have added more cold starts because fewer cached responses would be eligible, so in effect it might have worsened p99.
[07:33] Diego Alvarez: can we have an automated decision tree in the console? button that suggests rollback vs throttle?
[07:40] Maya Chen: that's a product idea — we can add to roadmap but not for the immediate pilot. we'll keep manual with SE recommendation.
[07:49] Priya Singh: on the topic of security and compliance, the customer legal team asked about whether extended trace logs include PII; do they?
[07:57] Rohit Patel: by default we mask PII in payloads per our data-retention policy, but for deeper troubleshooting we sometimes need unredacted samples. that requires a legal access request and KMS key access if stored encrypted.
[08:12] Lena Park: I'll own the legal flow for that.
[08:16] Marcus Lee: good. also, will we need SOC 2 attestation evidence for the change window?
[08:22] Maya Chen: Redwood can provide SOC 2 reports and our change approval logs, and we can export audit trails for the rollout.
[08:30] Diego Alvarez: perfect.
[08:33] Rohit Patel: technical deep-dive in the next section — observed metric plots: p50 stayed mostly flat, p95 rose 60ms, p99 spiked by 320ms; error rate peaked at 0.6% and was concentrated on the model decode path.
[08:51] Priya Singh: does that correlate with KV cache misses?
[08:55] Rohit Patel: yes ~82% of the affected traces had cache miss indicators.
[09:00] Maya Chen: in lay terms: if the model's namespace doesn't match the stored cache keys, it's like losing your warm context and every request has to reconstruct, hence latency and occasionally memory pressure leading to errors.
[09:16] Diego Alvarez: you mentioned memory pressure — did nodes OOM?
[09:20] Rohit Patel: not full OOM, but transient GC spikes and increased memory alloc which pushed a few containers over soft limits causing retries.
[09:29] Marcus Lee: we clipped those retries in SRE chart.
[09:33] Priya Singh: can we change retry policy or queue length to reduce retry storms?
[09:38] Rohit Patel: yes, recommended: backoff increase to 200ms->1s and max retries 2 for the route. lower retries reduce amplification.
[09:48] Maya Chen: noted as part of mitigation set.
[09:52] Diego Alvarez: any sign that the model weights themselves had a correctness issue?
[09:56] Rohit Patel: no, internal evals on a hidden testbed showed output quality comparable to v11. it's behavioral shift tied to cache behavior, not model corruption.
[10:07] Priya Singh: fine.
[10:09] Maya Chen: moving to observability gaps: we need a better end-to-end request id propagation, a larger trace sampler for problem routes, and faster ingestion for critical metrics.
[10:22] Rohit Patel: timeline: we'll add route-level trace sampler change, export per-shard logs, and surface a per-request KV cache key in debug mode.
[10:33] Diego Alvarez: please make sure sensitive fields are always redacted even in debug mode unless legal approves.
[10:39] Rohit Patel: agreed.
[10:41] Maya Chen: let's talk about the canary mechanicals: the canary will be launched with route flag prefix_cache_enabled=false for first 2 hours. we will also start synthetic requests at t=0 to warm models slowly.
[10:56] Marcus Lee: can synthetic traffic be made to mimic top 10 user flows? that's what our product metrics care about.
[11:02] Rohit Patel: yes we can parameterize the harness. we'll share config.
[11:07] Maya Chen: schedule — next steps: blue arc to upload samples by 02-09; Redwood posts finalized postmortem by 02-10; canary week target starting 02-16.
[11:20] Priya Singh: will engineering on-call be paged if the canary breaches thresholds?
[11:24] Rohit Patel: yes, we'll set threshold alerts and an automatic rollback policy which will also page.
[11:30] Diego Alvarez: on the rollback policy — any chance of false rollback due to noisy metrics?
[11:35] Rohit Patel: we use smoothed windows and require sustained breach over 5 minutes; still possible but unlikely.
[11:43] Maya Chen: decide, assign owners: Rohit owns metrics export and per-shard logs; Lena owns legal flow; Diego owns sample ingestion.
[11:54] Marcus Lee: one more ask — can you provide a simulated cost impact matrix for different batching and cache configurations? our finance team asks specifically about per-1M token delta.
[12:04] Rohit Patel: yes — Redwood Optimize team will run quick sim and produce a small table; I'll attach to the postmortem.
[12:13] Priya Singh: great.
[12:16] Maya Chen: any other risks we haven't covered?
[12:19] Marcus Lee: nothing major.
[12:21] Diego Alvarez: one micro item — canary cannot coincide with our planned DB migration same week; need to avoid windows.
[12:27] Maya Chen: acknowledgement — we'll coordinate calendar.
[12:30] Rohit Patel: closing notes: we'll push a postmortem draft by end of day tomorrow for comments.
[12:36] Maya Chen: ok thank you all, we have clear owners and dates. end of meeting.
[12:43] (call ends)
